title: How the zeros of deformed monotone Hurwitz polynomials approach their limits
shortTitle: Which way the zeros of Hurwitz polynomials move
oneLine: The second large-genus term settles the direction in the Coulter–Do–Moskovsky conjecture, and exact certificates cover every genus up to degree ten
abstract: Count the monotone transitive factorisations of a permutation of cycle type μ into transpositions, with a weight t for each distinct larger letter used. Coulter, Do and Moskovsky called the resulting polynomials deformed monotone Hurwitz numbers and conjectured that their zeros are real, interlace and, as the genus grows, converge to explicit limits from a definite side (their Conjecture 3.15). The limits follow from the leading large-genus term of Accadia, Lewański and Ruzza. This candidate computes the next term for every profile and for any finite list of profiles: it depends on the profile only through its number of fixed points. Its sign fixes the side and rate of approach of every zero, so the eventual form of Conjecture 3.15 holds, with an explicit genus threshold that is far from optimal. Monotone approach cannot start at genus zero in general: for two and for three 2-cycles some zeros first move away. For all 132 profiles of degrees 4 to 10, exact certificates prove real zeros at every genus and list exactly when a zero moves away from its limit: only 8 profiles, all made of even cycles, and never after genus 2. Further results give the third term (fixed points and 2-cycles), show that early terms depend only on short cycles, identify the limiting law of the larger letters used (letter b with probability (b−1)/(d−1), independently) and explain exact coincidences in the published tables. Limits: fixed degree and growing genus only; interlacing at small genus is not certified; the joint regime and the real-Grassmannian deformation remain open. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

evidence: A 17-page paper with a plain introduction (the problem, why it matters, what was known, what is new, an example and a map), written proofs of every theorem, checks, scope, open problems and an AI-use statement. Eight Python programs accompany it, all exact (Fractions and SymPy, with NumPy integer arithmetic) except 60-digit mpmath comparisons with published decimals: they check the second term for every profile of degrees 2 to 5, multi-profile cases, the third term, the fixed-point identity, the occupancy law, the census of all 132 profiles of degrees 4 to 10, and the comparison with the published tables. A clean replay in Python's optimised mode reproduced all eight recorded outputs byte for byte; altering the second-term coefficient makes the check fail; Linux CI reproduces the outputs exactly. Theorem 5.2 rests on the exact certificates of the census program.

keyResults: Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.2 (proof): for fixed d, the second term of the large-genus expansion is explicit for every profile and every finite list of profiles, and depends on a profile only through its number of fixed points.
Theorems 4.1 and 4.4 (proof): its sign gives the direction predicted by Coulter, Do and Moskovsky, so their Conjecture 3.15 holds in its eventual form; r ≥ 200 d² log(20d) suffices, far from optimal.
Theorem 5.1 (proof): monotone approach cannot start at genus 0 in general; for two and for three 2-cycles some zeros first move away from their limits.

Theorem 5.2 (exact certificates): for all 132 profiles of degrees 4 to 10 the zeros are real at every genus; exactly 8 profiles, all made of even cycles, have a zero moving away, and never after genus 2. Interlacing at small genus is not certified.

Theorems 6.1–6.2 and Proposition 7.2 (proof): the third term depends only on fixed points and 2-cycles, early terms see only short cycles, and in a long random factorisation letter b is used with probability (b−1)/(d−1), independently.

Credit and limits: limits and leading term are due to Accadia, Lewański and Ruzza; the t = 1 structure and the simple-Hurwitz fixed-point formula to Yang; the conjectures, tables and cut-and-join recursion (used for Proposition 4.5) to Coulter, Do and Moskovsky. Fixed degree, growing genus only.
